remarks_1999: Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Cow trying to get apples on tree near shed at Lake George." Backing inscription dates 1921. Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks date 1922. Pictured in 1923 New York (Anderson) Stieglitz installation photographs, see Appendix III, figures 12, 20, 21. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_post_1999:
In addition to understanding the principles of painting, O’Keeffe knew and understood cows. She was raised on a dairy farm in Wisconsin and Spent time in Rural Virginia and Texas. She painted this cow when she was summering at her husband’s family farm in Lake George, New York, in 1921. O’Keeffe has balanced the “cow-ness” of her subject—its liquid eye and soft tongue—with the “visual music” of an undulating black-and-white pyramid, defined at the bottom by the ovals of eye and jaw and at the apex by the arcs of tongue and grapes. 
(Text pulled from The First Hundred Years  label for an exhibition in 2015.) (Source: Denver Art Museum, 2025)

description: A black and brown cow's head with a curling pink tongue is oriented vertically and seen in profile. The cow has a large eye with a black pupil. It appears to be licking some small, dark green, circular objects at the top of the narrow composition. The background is painted light green.
title: Cow Licking
